preview: Samsung R&D internship interview experience by Saurav Kanegaonkar, consisting of an online coding test, a technical round, and a technical + HR round.
content: Samsung R&D Interview Experience (Internship) Saurav Kanegaonkar | T.Y. B.Tech CE 2018-22 Samsung R&D had visited our college (virtually xD). The process consisted of 3 rounds- an online coding test, a Technical round and a Technical + HR round. Round 1 was on 6th October, 2020 at 9am and the interviews were on 8th October, 2020 from 4:30pm onwards. 1) Round 1- Online test - 70 minutes ●It was conducted on cocubes platform where we had to enable our laptop’s camera and we were not allowed to switch tabs/windows. ●We were given 3 coding questions to solve in 70 minutes. ●C#, C++ and Java were the only options for the choice of language. ●The first question was for 3 points and the other 2 questions were for 5 points each. ●We had to write the code in the given function only and we weren’t allowed to modify any other part of the code. ●We could not see which header files were included or the input format, so there was some confusion whether STL was included or not, but some people could use strings, queue data structure. The questions which appeared on my set where: i. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/rearrange-positive-and-negative-number/ ii.https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/smallest-number-in-bst-which-is-greater-than-or-equal-to-n/ iii.https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/build-lowest-number-by-removing-n-digits-from-a-given-number/ The catch with the last question was that they had given a character array as a parameter instead of a string so it was quite difficult to play with. Luckily, I was allowed to use strings and I solved the sum. Some questions which were asked on other sets: i. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sum-of-cousins-of-a-given-node-in-a-binary-tree/ ii.https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-possible-words-phone-digits/ - in this question, participants were supposed to fill the given 2 dimensional character array provided in the form of double pointer (from the parameters) and return it instead of printing each combination directly. Because of this most of the students who got this set couldn’t solve this question. Out of the 4 branches (CS, IT, Electronics, and EXTC) only 9 got selected for the interviews and I was one of them. Students who had solved all the 3 sums were selected for the next round. 2) Round 2- Technical round ~ 40 minutes The video call was conducted on Skype. The interviewer was very friendly and asked me to introduce myself. He asked questions related to college fests like Pratibimb as I had mentioned in my resume that I was the Chief Theatrical Manager (CTM) of Mumbai’s Got Talent. Then he moved on to my resume and asked that if I had to scale any of my projects then how would I do it? I answered this by explaining the types of scaling (Horizontal or Vertical Scaling) and which would be more effective according to the budget given. He then asked what would happen if 2 users were trying to book an airline ticket (I had mentioned a project based on an Airline Management System in my resume) at the same time, what measures would I take? It was an Operating System question related to Race Condition and how process synchronisation will help. He also asked me to give the examples of process synchronisation methods and I couldn’t remember. He gave me a small hint which helped me to give him the answer. He was quite satisfied with my answers. He asked which coding problem I found difficult to solve recently. I told him about the Trie data structure. I explained it’s functionality, implementation and where it’s used in real world applications. He then proceeded by giving me a coding question. I had seen this question earlier and I knew the answer BUT I did not give him the optimised answer directly knowing that he’ll ask me more complex coding questions xD. So first I gave him a naive approach and then we both started to optimise my solution and then I gave him the optimised solution. Doing this is necessary because the interviewer is interested in how we think and how we can come up to the optimised solution with some help instead of giving direct answers. The interviewer was helping me in each step and then I was asked to code on Google docs. He was satisfied with my answer. At the end he asked me whether I had any questions for him and I asked his job profile and his experience/projects up till now. After answering my question, he told me then and there that I’m selected for round 3. Out of the 9, 6 were selected for round 3. 3) Round 3 - Technical + HR ~ 35 minutes The interviewer was at senior post level and was friendly while taking the interview. He asked me to introduce myself and to explain any 1 project thoroughly. While I was explaining, he asked me follow up questions of which I could answer easily. Then he asked me questions related stl: ●map vs unordered_map, brief explanation of internal working of each ●Friend 1 has 500 friends, friend 2 has 1000 friends on facebook, how will you find the mutual friends? ●What is hashing? Different types of hashing? ●How does a map work? ●What are vectors, what’s the internal working of a vector? The interviewer asked me why I haven’t done any projects on ML/DL. The reason I gave was that I had done some ML/DL projects earlier and it’s been time that I haven’t done ML/DL, for that reason I did not include it in the resume. The actual reason was that I was selected for previous companies interviews and I couldn’t answer ML/DL questions as they asked deeper concepts which I was unaware about. And for that reason I had removed projects, languages, topics from my resume that I haven’t done for a long time. It’s my request that you shouldn’t add languages that you haven’t done for a while/ don't have much confidence in. It’s not necessary that your resume is filled with lots of projects and you have learned many languages because they are going to question you about everything you have mentioned in your resume. So luckily the interviewer did not ask me any questions related to ML/DL and guided me to do ML/DL in the remaining 2 years of my college as it may impress the interviewer more but he said that he was impressed with my answers and resume. The 3rd round was completed by 7PM and I had to wait for 4 hours for the result which was more exhausting than the interviews xDD. 6 students were selected for Samsung R&D in Bangalore and I was one of them.
